tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

   `docs/darwin-remote-builder.md`;
5. on exit, however it exits: runs `install/finalize-ssh.sh` (disables sshd

content.text:
Correct — setsuna doesn't need one, and it's already two-thirds out:

- `3f5d7887` moved it into the cluster ssh group (`yui mio meiko setsuna ritsu mugi azusa`)
- `09a7408c` took it out of the secrets fleet
- it was **never** in `wifHosts`/`wifTpmHosts`, so it's irrelevant to item 4

**On mari:** I can't verify it from here, and not because of setsuna. mari doesn't resolve from shiori (no ssh config entry, no DNS), and per `README.md:60` it has no CI job — `hms` falls back to a local build there. So mari can only be activated on mari itself. The config is right (its eval suite is 4/4 on current master); whether it's *applied* is only answerable on the machine.

**What pulling setsuna out touches** — 13 tracked files. Three tiers:

1. **The entry itself:** `flake.nix:95-99` (`homeConfigurations.setsuna`).
2. **A live cost:** `.forgejo/workflows/nix-home.yml:167` builds `setsuna.activationPackage` on every run. Pure waste today.
3. **Mechanical list/comment edits:** `home.nix` (56, 103, 157, 225, 1119, 1459, 1703, plus the kanshi profile at 3645-3659), `hyprland.nix:111`, `system/deploy:85`, `system/packages.shiori:50`, `nix-eval.yml:127`, and 5 docs.

**Two spots are decisions, not deletions:**

- `home.nix:172` — `viaDconf = hostname == "setsuna"`. setsuna is the **only** dconf host, so removing it makes the flag permanently false and the `dconf.settings` scaling branch dead. The comment at `home.nix:3817` says gating `dconf.enable` on the setsuna hostname cost something once, so I'd delete `viaDconf` and its branch but leave `dconf.enable` alone.
- `tests/polkit-agent.sh:239` — setsuna is the "other gui host" case, the one that catches a gui host silently losing the polkit unit. I'd repoint it at fujiwara (also `gui = true`).

Also worth noting `home.nix:1703`'s host list is already stale independently of this — it says "six hosts: utsuho, kyuusaku, setsuna, shiori, fujiwara and mari", missing chiyari.

~30-40 min including re-running the eval suites, which are the slow part.

Next, under two minutes: say go and I'll start with `nix-home.yml:167` — dropping the CI target is zero-risk and independent of both decisions above.

# TDD

## Overview

**Test-first, always.** Write the failing test before the code it covers, watch
it fail, then write the minimal code to make it pass. A test you never saw fail
proves nothing — it may pass for the wrong reason, or not exercise the behavior
at all.

Keep the test scoped to the interfaces you are actually changing — a test that
drifts wider stops being a contract anyone can rely on. Inside a drovr phase
this also binds the next phase's contract.

## The cycle

1. **RED** — write the failing test named in the task's verification. Run it.
   *Watch it fail*, and confirm it fails for the reason you expect (missing
   behavior, not a typo or compile error elsewhere).
2. **GREEN** — write the *minimal* code to make that test pass. No extra
   features, no speculative abstraction — just enough to go green.
3. **REFACTOR** — clean up with the test as your safety net, re-running it.

Repeat per behavior. One failing test at a time.

## Red flags — STOP

- Wrote code before the test → delete it, start with the test.
- "I'll add the test after" → tests-after check *what the code does*, not what it
  *should* do. Test first.
- Test passed the first time you ran it → you never saw RED; make sure it truly
  exercises the new behavior.
- Test is scoped wider than this task's interfaces → tighten it; drift breaks the
  contract the next phase inherits.

## Verifying the pass

Green on the one test is necessary, not sufficient. Before claiming done, hand
off to `drovr:verification-before-completion` — run the full suite and the build,
and confirm with evidence, not assertion.

input.command:
cat > /home/sauyon/devel/.worktrees/dotfiles-setsuna/tests/host-inventory.sh <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Cases for the repo's host lists agreeing with the configurations that exist.
#
# `flake.nix`'s `homeConfigurations` is the only authority on which hosts this
# repo builds. Six other places repeat that set by hand, because reading the
# flake costs a full evaluation and three of the six are shell running on a box
# mid-activation:
#
#   home.nix  archHosts          the Arch-specific package/deploy paths
#   home.nix  hms's CI case       which hosts have a nix-home.yml job
#   home.nix  hmeval's all_hosts  which hosts get evaluated
#   system/deploy's case          which hosts enable multilib
#   nix-home.yml                  which activationPackages CI actually builds
#   home.nix  wifHosts/wifTpmHosts the WIF device-identity fleet
#
# A hand-copied set drifts in two directions and both are silent. A host that
# exists but is missing from a list never gets built, evaluated or deployed --
# `hmeval`'s own comment says so ("Out of step with flake.nix => a host silently
# never gets checked, so keep them together") and then nothing enforced it. A
# host that is in a list but no longer exists is worse than noise: CI spends a
# build slot per run on it, and `nix build` on a missing attribute fails the
# whole job, so one decommission can red every run until someone reads the log.
#
# Why exact set equality rather than a subset for cases 2-4: archHosts, hms's
# case and nix-home.yml's targets are three spellings of one fact -- "the Linux
# hosts CI builds". A subset check passes while two of them disagree, which is
# the state this file exists to catch.
#
# wifHosts is checked as a subset instead, deliberately: it is a different fact
# (which hosts have a published JWK) and mari is in it while having no CI job at
# all. wifTpmHosts ⊆ wifHosts is the real constraint there -- a host keeping its
# key in the TPM must first be enrolled, and the reverse order mints a key
# nothing authorises.
#
#   ./tests/host-inventory.sh
set -u

repo="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"

fails=0; n=0
ok()  { n=$((n+1)); printf 'ok %d - %s\n' "$n" "$1"; }
bad() { n=$((n+1)); fails=$((fails+1)); printf 'FAIL %d - %s\n' "$n" "$1"; }

# Every reader below is a grep, and a grep that matches nothing returns the
# empty string -- which compares equal to another empty string. That is exactly
# how tests/sops-recipients.sh once reported two green checks off a yq that was
# writing nothing at all, so an empty read is a failure here, never a match.
same() { # same <label> <got> <want>
  if [ -z "$2" ] || [ -z "$3" ]; then
    bad "$1"$'\n'"      read nothing: one side came back empty, so nothing was compared."$'\n'"      want: ${3:-<empty>}"$'\n'"      got:  ${2:-<empty>}"
  elif [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then
    ok "$1"
  else
    bad "$1"$'\n'"      want: $3"$'\n'"      got:  $2"
  fi
}

# subset <label> <needles> <haystack> -- every word of $2 appears in $3.
subset() {
  if [ -z "$2" ] || [ -z "$3" ]; then
    bad "$1"$'\n'"      read nothing: one side came back empty, so nothing was compared."
    return
  fi
  local missing=""
  for h in $2; do
    case " $3 " in *" $h "*) ;; *) missing="$missing $h" ;; esac
  done
  if [ -z "$missing" ]; then ok "$1"
  else bad "$1"$'\n'"      not in $4:$missing"; fi
}

# Sort and space-join, so a list's order is never the thing that fails.
norm() { tr -s ' |",[]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//'; }

# ── the authority ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A failure to evaluate is a failure of the case, not a reason to skip: a flake
# that does not evaluate is the regression these lists are copied from.
err=$(mktemp); trap 'rm -f "$err"' EXIT
HOSTS=$(nix eval --json "$repo#homeConfigurations" --apply builtins.attrNames 2>"$err" \
          | tr -d '[]"' | tr ',' '\n' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')
if [ -z "$HOSTS" ]; then
  echo "FAIL 1 - flake.nix#homeConfigurations evaluates" >&2
  sed 's/^/      /' "$err" >&2
  echo; echo "1 check, 1 failed"
  exit 1
fi
ok "flake.nix#homeConfigurations evaluates ($HOSTS)"

# ── the six copies ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
line()  { grep -m1 -E "$1" "$2"; }

arch=$(line '^ +archHosts = \[' "$repo/home.nix"      | sed 's/.*\[//' | norm)
hmsci=$(line '^ +[a-z]+(\|[a-z]+)+\) ;;' "$repo/home.nix" | norm)
hmeval=$(line '^ +all_hosts="' "$repo/home.nix"       | sed 's/.*="//;s/"//' | norm)
deploy=$(line '^[a-z]+( \| [a-z]+)+\)' "$repo/system/deploy" | norm)
ciblt=$(grep -oE 'homeConfigurations\.[a-z]+\.activationPackage' \
          "$repo/.forgejo/workflows/nix-home.yml" | sed 's/homeConfigurations\.//;s/\.activationPackage//' | norm)
wif=$(line '^ +wifHosts = \[' "$repo/home.nix"        | sed 's/.*\[//' | norm)
wiftpm=$(line '^ +wifTpmHosts = \[' "$repo/home.nix"  | sed 's/.*\[//' | norm)

# hmeval claims to cover every configuration, so it is the one exact match
# against the flake rather than against the Linux-CI set.
same "hmeval's all_hosts covers exactly the configurations that exist" "$hmeval" "$HOSTS"

# The three spellings of "the Linux hosts CI builds".
same "hms's CI-job case matches archHosts" "$hmsci" "$arch"
same "nix-home.yml builds exactly archHosts" "$ciblt" "$arch"
same "system/deploy's multilib case matches archHosts" "$deploy" "$arch"

# Each list names only hosts that exist.
subset "every archHosts entry is a real configuration" "$arch" "$HOSTS" "homeConfigurations"
subset "every wifHosts entry is a real configuration" "$wif" "$HOSTS" "homeConfigurations"
# Enrolment precedes key storage: a TPM host must already have a published JWK.
subset "every wifTpmHosts entry is also in wifHosts" "$wiftpm" "$wif" "wifHosts"

echo
if [ "$fails" = 0 ]; then echo "$n checks, all good"; else echo "$n checks, $fails failed"; fi
[ "$fails" = 0 ]
SCRIPT

# The unit is generated identically for every desktop host, so checking only
# shiori leaves the other gui hosts unmeasured. This catches a gui host that
# silently loses the unit; the vendor mapping is covered by the utsuho block below.
echo "evaluating fujiwara (gui = true)"
present=$(has_unit fujiwara) ||
  die "could not evaluate systemd.user.services for fujiwara (see the nix error above)"
if [ "$present" = true ]; then
  ok "fujiwara, the other gui host, defines the unit too"
else
  no "fujiwara, the other gui host, defines the unit too" "no unit on a gui = true host"
fi

# utsuho is the only gui host that declares a gpu (amd), and glWrapper refuses any
# gpu it has no mapping for. Note what `has_unit` can and cannot tell us here: it
# is a membership test (`ss ? hyprpolkitagent`) and never forces ExecStart, so a
# throw from the gpu mapping is invisible to it. Only forcing the unit itself --
# the unit_json below -- can surface that, which is why this block asserts through
# that path and dies on its failure rather than folding it into a case.
#
# What is being pinned is the mesa-covers-amd assumption: radeonsi ships in mesa's
# own lib/dri, so amd must land on the *same* nixgl attr as Intel. The literal
# `nixGLIntel` is deliberate -- matching any `nixGL*` would let a future second
# branch map amd onto a proprietary wrapper and still pass.
echo "evaluating utsuho (gui = true, gpu = amd)"
present=$(has_unit utsuho) ||
  die "could not evaluate systemd.user.services for utsuho (see the nix error above)"
vendor_label="utsuho (gpu = amd) dispatches to nixGLIntel, the mesa wrapper"
if [ "$present" = true ]; then
  ok "utsuho, the gui host declaring a gpu, defines the unit"
  # Only inside this branch: if the unit is absent, forcing it would abort the run
  # on a missing attribute and blame the gpu mapping for it -- taking the remaining
  # cases and the summary line down with it.
  u_unit=$(unit_json utsuho) ||
    die "could not evaluate utsuho's hyprpolkitagent unit -- if the error above names nixGL, the gpu mapping rejected \"amd\""
  u_exec=$(python3 -c '
import json,sys
v=(json.loads(sys.argv[1]).get("Service") or {}).get("ExecStart")
if isinstance(v,list): v = v[0] if len(v)==1 else ""
print(v or "")
' "$u_unit") || die "could not read utsuho's ExecStart out of the unit JSON"
  shim_execs_vendor "$u_exec" "nixGLIntel" "$vendor_label"
else
  no "utsuho, the gui host declaring a gpu, defines the unit" "no unit on a gui = true host"
  no "$vendor_label" "skipped: utsuho has no unit to read an ExecStart from"
fi

# glWrapper's two consumers, tested through the linkage rather than through a real
# host's value. Pinning `defaultWrapper = "mesa"` on shiori/utsuho looked like it
# guarded this and did not: "mesa" is *home-manager's own default*, so those cases
# passed identically with the assignment deleted -- vacuous in exactly the spot
# where the two halves had already drifted apart once.
#
# So inject a synthetic machine instead. extendModules can override the
# extraSpecialArgs `machine` that flake.nix passes in, which gives a host that does
# not exist without touching flake.nix: gpu = "nvidia" must be refused by BOTH

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /nix/store/REDACTED/skills/code-review

# Code Review

## Overview

**They find, you fix.** Follow the spirit, not the letter: dispatching a
reviewer satisfies the letter; one that read an empty diff, or that you never
waited for, looked at nothing and found nothing. The rule is that
somebody who did not write the change has said what is wrong with it — and that
cannot be you. You read the change you meant to make, not the one on disk.

**Write for the agent who inherits this: the next phase agent is you, with your
context gone.** A finding you settled in your head is one they meet as a bug,
with nothing saying anyone saw it.

## The Iron Law

```
NO CHANGE IS DONE UNTIL A READ-ONLY REVIEWER HAS SEEN IT AND
EVERY CRITICAL AND IMPORTANT FINDING IS RESOLVED OR RECORDED AS DEFERRED.
```

**Read-only** is a trust boundary, not a performance note: the reviewer reads
anything, runs read-only checks, and writes nothing — not source, not git, not
run state. You stay the single writer.

No exceptions. The first names its addressee; the rest hold for anyone.

- **Never run a reviewer in the background — you, the agent in a herdr pane,
  where ending a turn *is* how you report done.** Do not set
  `run_in_background`, do not yield, and do not schedule a wakeup while one is
  out. A backgrounded reviewer parks you mid-turn, indistinguishable from a
  finished turn, and the run stalls until a human nudges the pane. Dispatch it
  blocking and read its verdict in the turn you dispatched it. That reason is
  role-specific, so there is exactly one role it does not bind: the **driver**,
  which backgrounds the panel and ends the turn because its harness re-invokes
  it on process exit — `skills/pipeline/SKILL.md` says so at its own loop. A
  split by role, not a preference. In a pane, the prohibition is yours.
- **Do not judge a change too small to review.** A one-line edit to a condition
  is the size this skill exists for. Dispatch a reviewer over it.
- **Do not count your own read as the review.** Re-reading your diff tells you
  it matches what you intended — the one thing never in doubt. Dispatch someone
  who does not know it.
- **Do not leave it for the pipeline's review phase.** That phase reads what you
  hand it, after later work is built on it. Dispatch here, while the change is
  one commit wide.
- **Do not close a finding by disagreeing with it.** When you will not fix one,
  quote it and write the reason in the report or handoff. An unrecorded
  decision reads downstream like an unread finding.
- **Do not repeat a verdict you have not read.** Open the file the reviewer
  names, or re-run the review when it named none. A reviewer that never came
  back has not said "clean".

## Announce

Say this out loud before dispatching anything:

```
Using drovr:code-review — dispatching read-only reviewers before calling this done.
```

## The procedure

> When a skill or briefing gives you a numbered checklist, create **one tracked item per step**
> using whatever task tool this harness exposes — `TodoWrite`, or `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` —
> before you start step 1. Mark each in-progress when you start it and complete when its
> evidence is in hand. If the harness exposes no task tool, write the checklist to
> `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<run>/checklist.md` when inside a run, or `CHECKLIST.md` at the
> repo root otherwise, and tick items there. An untracked checklist decays with the context
> window; that decay is the exact failure drovr exists to fight.

Re-create those items for each change you review, not once for the session.

1. **Write down the change and the exact range** — the files, and `<base>..HEAD`.
   Get it wrong and the reviewer reports clean on nothing.
2. **Dispatch read-only reviewers, blocking, one per angle:** run
   `drovr code-review run <run> <task>` (`<base>` from `<task>-base.sha`, recorded
   before your first edit) — or, **inline** with no run,
   `drovr code-review run --base "$(git merge-base HEAD main)" <task>`. Nothing
   else, and never invent a run to get one.

   It spawns one reviewer per **configured** angle — `config.angles`, which
   defaults to correctness, security, error-handling, type-design — each writing
   `<task>-review-<angle>.json`, merged into `<task>-review.json`. **Read the
   config, not this page**, and cover any lens it omits yourself.

   Tell each reviewer to review as a skeptic, not the author; to say whether the
   tests exercise the behaviour, not just that they pass; to rate every finding
   **Critical, Important or nit** — what the Iron Law gates on — and say so when
   it found none; and to write them to a path you name, so step 3 has something
   to open. The lenses to cover:
   - **Spec compliance** — what was agreed, no more, no less?
   - **Correctness** — real bugs, unhandled cases, broken invariants.
   - **Verification** — do the claimed tests exist, and would they fail on a
     regression?
   - **Quality** — reuse, simplification, consistency with the code around it.
3. **Wait for every reviewer, then read what each wrote.** Open the findings
   file by path, then classify the round by how the panel exited:

   | Exit | What it means |
   |---|---|
   | 0 | clean — a real range was reviewed, nothing blocking |
   | 3 | blocking findings; go to step 5 |
   | 2 | timeout — reviewers are slow, not broken. Re-run the same command: it resumes the panel in flight |
   | 1 | error, or an empty `<base>..HEAD` it refused. Fix the range or the setup; never re-run blindly |
   | 137/143 | **your own harness killed it.** drovr produced no verdict at all, and none of the rows above describes the run. Re-run to resume, and record the round as **unclassifiable** — never as a timeout |

   A reviewer that returned no verdict is none of the five: re-dispatch rather
   than report its silence.

   **Only 0 is clean, and one clean round does not end the loop.** Stop at
   whichever of three comes first:
   - **Two consecutive clean rounds over an unchanged HEAD.** Any edit between
     them resets the count — the second round is evidence about the first only
     if it read the same code.
   - **A cap of six rounds**, which is *not* a clean ending: write up every
     round's verdict and everything still open (step 5), and finish on that
     record rather than on a verdict. Only rounds that delivered every
     configured angle count toward the cap — a missing angle is a Critical
     stand-in, so a round that lost a reviewer never measured the code.
   - **Two consecutive rounds that lost a dimension** — its own outcome,
     neither clean nor the cap: the panel is failing to deliver and further
     rounds are not measuring the code. Name the angles that never ran. Without
     this the loop cannot end at all, since such a round is never clean and
     never counts toward the cap.

   Three caveats the rule owes you. Two cleans make a false clean **less
   likely**, not unlikely, and prove nothing about convergence — in forge#88's
   own data two consecutive cleans preceded a `changes` round with seven
   findings. **Six is a starting number, revisable on evidence**, not a
   principled constant. And every word of this is prose nothing enforces — the
   shape of the *"re-run it"* that produced 47 re-arms over 14 hours.
4. **Check what the reviewer actually read — range *and* working tree.** The
   range must be the whole of `<base>..HEAD`, every file you touched, not a
   subset you picked; **and uncommitted work is in scope, not exempt** — drovr's
   panel reviews the diff *plus the current working tree*. A verdict covers what
   is on disk only if the reviewer saw both. Clean on an empty range, a subset,
   or a tree with unreviewed edits in it is about a change nobody read.
5. **Resolve every Critical and Important finding, or record the deferral with
   `drovr code-review defer`.** Per finding: quote it, then name the edit
   answering it by file — or, if you are not making it, run

   ```
   drovr code-review defer <RUN> <TASK> --file <path> [--line <n>] \
     --severity <critical|important|nit> --summary "<the finding>" \
     --reason "<why it is not being fixed>"
   ```

   A deferral written only in prose is one the next round cannot read, so it
   re-raises the finding you already ruled on. The command appends to a
   per-task log every later seed carries; prose does not.
6. **Re-run the checks after your last review-driven edit, then say it is
   done.** The fixes are new, unverified code: run the tests. When the change is
   not code and has no suite, name what you re-read instead and why it covers the
   edits — written down, never assumed. Report the findings, the edits and the
   deferrals; inside a drovr phase this also gates `drovr phase done`. **Done is
   step 3's termination rule met, not the first exit 0** — say which of the
   three ended it, and on the cap or a lost dimension say plainly that the loop
   ended on a record rather than on a clean verdict.

## Requirements

The middle column is what the claim takes; the right is what gets accepted
instead.

| The claim | Required evidence | NOT sufficient |
|---|---|---|
| *"This change has been reviewed"* | A read-only reviewer dispatched over this change in the foreground, returned in this turn, and the range you handed it, written down | Your own re-read · a reviewer launched and not waited for · a review of the tree before your last edit |
| *"The reviewer found nothing"* | The findings file it wrote, opened by path and read by you — or the review re-run by you when it wrote none — **and** what it read shown to be the whole of `<base>..HEAD` **plus your working tree** | Its summary, however much output it pastes · exit 1 or 2 · a subset of your files · uncommitted edits nobody looked at · a verdict that never arrived |
| *"Every Critical and Important finding is resolved"* | Each quoted, the edit answering it named by file, and step 6's checks re-run after the last edit | A count · agreeing with one in prose · fixing the Criticals and leaving the Importants |
| *"That finding does not apply here"* | The finding quoted, and the reason written where the next agent reads it | Deciding it in your head · *"out of scope"* with no scope named · silence, which downstream reads as resolved |

## Red flags — STOP

Some are thoughts, some are things you have just written. Either way you are at
the line.

- *"They are going to read it line by line anyway."* · *"The lead said just
  send it."* · *"It is a two-line change."* · *"I already reviewed it myself."*
  · *"The pipeline's review phase will catch it."* — each opens a row in
  *Rationalizations*, verbatim. Go do the thing in its row.
- *You are about to launch a reviewer in the background and keep working.* →
  Dispatch it blocking. No version of that ends with you reading its verdict
  this turn.
- *A reviewer has not come back and you are writing the report.* → Block on it.
  Silence is not a pass; a parked reviewer is not a finished one.
- *The panel came back clean in seconds on a large diff.* → Check what it read.
  Clean and empty look identical from here.
- **Anything that treats the change as finished** — any wording at all, and
  also committing, opening a PR, or starting the next task — while a reviewer is
  unread, unreturned, or holding an unresolved Critical or Important finding. If
  you cannot name the reviewer and point at what it wrote, change what you
  dispatched, not how you word it.

## Rationalizations

The right column is an instruction, not an argument. Do the thing in it.

| The thought | Do this instead |
|---|---|
| *"They are going to read it line by line anyway."* | Dispatch the reviewer first, then send it. Two different reads: theirs is for fit, the review's is for correctness, and one does not make the other redundant — reading a document aloud catches prose gaps, not retry semantics. |
| *"The lead said just send it."* | Send it after the review, and tell them the call moves. That is a scheduling reflex, not anyone weighing the technical risk — the calendar is theirs, the correctness yours. |
| *"It is a two-line change."* | Dispatch a reviewer over the two lines. Size is not a risk measure, and the risk you estimate in order to skip the review is what it would have told you. |
| *"I already reviewed it myself."* | Dispatch one that did not write it. Your read confirms the diff matches your intent; the defects worth catching are in what you did not think of. |
| *"The pipeline's review phase will catch it."* | Dispatch here, now. That phase reads what you hand it, after later tasks built on it; a finding costs more at every step it survives. |
| *"The reviewer came back with no findings."* | Open the file it named, and check it read your whole change, working tree included. An empty range comes back clean from every angle at once. |

## Worked example

One read away, in `skills/code-review/worked-example.md`: a 320-line spec, a
client call in 19 minutes, a $45,000 sign-off and a lead writing *"just send
it"* — the rationalization refused, the panel run, two Importants found, the
call moved 22 minutes. Worth reading once; the rules above do not depend on it.

## Cross-refs

- `drovr:verification-before-completion` — REQUIRED before you repeat a
  verdict: a reviewer's report is a claim, not evidence.
- `drovr:systematic-debugging` — REQUIRED when a finding is a bug: it is a

content.content:
/home/sauyon/.nix-profile/bin/drovr
Spawn one review panel for `task`, wait, merge, exit 0/3/2/1.

Two forms:

```text drovr code-review run <RUN> <TASK>                    # inside a pipeline run drovr code-review run --base <rev> [--dir <repo>] <TASK>   # anywhere else ```

The second exists because `drovr:code-review` is unconditional while `drovr:using-drovr`'s escalation contract says to work INLINE until the work outgrows one context — so the agent that followed the contract correctly was the one with no run, and no way to review its change (forge#108). `--base` supplies what `<TASK>-base.sha` supplies in a run, so nothing has to have been recorded before the first edit: after the fact you know your own branch point, `git merge-base HEAD main`. `--dir` defaults to the current directory.

The panel, the brief, the resume and the merged findings are identical between the two; only the ADDRESSING changes. content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /nix/store/REDACTED/skills/systematic-debugging

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

**A fix you cannot explain is a guess wearing a diff.** Until the failure
happens on demand and you can say *mechanistically* why, any change you make is
as likely to hide the bug as to remove it. Follow the spirit, not the letter:
running the reproduction once, seeing red, and then fixing what you *assumed*
was wrong satisfies the ordering and proves nothing. The rule is that the cause
you fix is the cause you demonstrated.

**Write for the agent who inherits this: the next phase agent is you, with your
context gone.** They will not have your hunch, your scrollback, or the shape you
recognized. They get the reproduction command, the cause you wrote down, and the
test you added — anything you only knew is lost at the phase boundary.

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIX BEFORE A REPRODUCTION AND A MECHANISTIC CAUSE.
```

No exceptions:

- **Do not act on a shape you recognize.** A failure matching one you have seen
  before is a reason to *suspect* a cause, not a reason to skip confirming it.
  Go read this instance's fixture, input, or state and confirm it is that bug.
  Recognition works on the assertion output; the bug lives somewhere you have
  not looked yet.
- **Do not read a conditional instruction as permission to skip its condition.**
  *"If it's the off-by-one, just fix it"* waives re-litigating the fix once the
  cause is confirmed — it never waives confirming it. Establish the antecedent
  yourself, then take the permission it grants.
- **Do not let a deadline shorten the verification.** After the fix, re-run the
  original trigger **and** the full suite — the scope
  `drovr:verification-before-completion` defines, not one you pick under time
  pressure. The clock does not change which tests can catch what this fix
  disturbed. If the full suite genuinely cannot be run here, name the exact
  command you did not run and do not report the bug as fixed.
- **Do not start fix #4.** Three *failed fixes* — the unit is defined in step 6 —
  means your model of the system is wrong, not that the fourth guess is due.
  Stop, say so, and question the design with whoever owns it before changing
  another line.
- **Do not substitute reasoning for a reproduction.** If you cannot trigger the
  failure on demand, that is the finding to report. Keep narrowing — smaller
  input, more logging, a read-only explorer — and stop before shipping a fix
  you cannot verify.

## Announce

Say this out loud when you start, before the first edit:

```
Using drovr:systematic-debugging — reproducing before fixing.
```

## The procedure

> When a skill or briefing gives you a numbered checklist, create **one tracked item per step**
> using whatever task tool this harness exposes — `TodoWrite`, or `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` —
> before you start step 1. Mark each in-progress when you start it and complete when its
> evidence is in hand. If the harness exposes no task tool, write the checklist to
> `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<run>/checklist.md` when inside a run, or `CHECKLIST.md` at the
> repo root otherwise, and tick items there. An untracked checklist decays with the context
> window; that decay is the exact failure drovr exists to fight.

Re-create those items for each bug you work, not once for the session. If you
fall back to `CHECKLIST.md` at a repo root, do not commit it.

1. **Reproduce.** Get a reliable, minimal trigger and record the exact command
   and its output. A bug you cannot reproduce on demand is a bug you cannot
   prove you fixed.
2. **Isolate.** Narrow to the smallest input, file, or code path that still
   shows it. Bisect, add logging, or dispatch a **read-only explorer** to map
   the suspect area. Fan-out investigation belongs to read-only explorers (e.g.
   `explore-mcp`), never to parallel writers — you keep the editing, which is
   what keeps drovr's single-writer rule intact.
3. **Root-cause.** Explain *why* it happens, mechanistically. "Adding this line
   makes it go away" is not a cause. Keep going until the explanation predicts
   the observed behavior exactly — including the parts you were not chasing.
4. **Fix.** Make the minimal change that addresses the cause, not the symptom.
5. **Verify.** Re-run your original trigger and confirm it is gone, then run the
   **full suite** — unconditionally, whatever the clock says.
   `drovr:verification-before-completion` owns what "full" means here and what
   evidence it takes; do not substitute a narrower scope you picked yourself.
   Add or fix a test that would have caught it.
6. **Escalate at three failed fixes.** A **failed fix** is one change you made,
   ran, and watched leave the failure in place. That is the unit — not edits, not
   builds, not ideas you considered and dropped. Count them for this one failure.
   At three, stop and question the design with whoever owns it; do not start fix
   #4 without that conversation. A run of wrong fixes is evidence about your
   model of the system, not about the next fix.

### The cycle

```dot
digraph debugging_loop {
  rankdir=LR;
  node [shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor=white];

  repro  [label="reproduce it\non demand", shape=diamond, fillcolor=lightyellow];
  story  [label="no trigger —\nyou have a story,\nnot a bug"];
  cause  [label="mechanistic cause", shape=diamond, fillcolor=lightyellow];
  fix    [label="minimal fix,\nat the cause", fillcolor=palegreen];
  verify [label="trigger +\nthe full suite", shape=diamond, fillcolor=lightyellow];
  stop   [label="three failed fixes —\nquestion the design", fillcolor=lightpink];
  // "failed fix" is procedure step 6's unit: a change made, run, and seen to
  // leave the failure in place.
  done   [label="fixed, with a test\nthat would have caught it"];

  repro  -> story  [label="cannot"];
  story  -> repro  [label="narrow: smaller input,\nlogging, read-only explorer"];
  repro  -> cause  [label="on demand"];
  cause  -> cause  [label="'it goes away' is\nnot a cause"];
  cause  -> fix    [label="predicts the\nobserved behavior"];
  fix    -> verify;
  verify -> done   [label="gone, suite green"];
  verify -> cause  [label="still failing —\ncount one failed fix"];
  verify -> stop   [label="that was the\nthird failed fix"];
}
```

## Red flags — STOP

Some of these are thoughts and some are things you have just observed. Either
way you are at the line, not past it — stop here and the loop is still intact.

- *"We've seen this exact failure before."* · *"They said if it's the off-by-one,
  just fix it."* · *"I'll run the broader suite if time allows."* — each of these
  opens a row in *Rationalizations* below. Go do the thing in its row.
- *You are editing code and have not yet run the failing command yourself.* →
  Run it first. What you are fixing is a description of the bug, not the bug.
- *The failure went away and you cannot say why.* → Put the change back and
  confirm it returns. A fix whose mechanism you cannot state may be moving the
  bug rather than removing it.
- *The failure is intermittent, so you will "fix it and watch".* → You have no
  trigger, so you will have no proof. Narrow until it is on demand, or report
  that you could not.
- *You are about to start a fourth fix for the same failure.* → Stop. Three
  failed fixes is the escalation trigger, not a streak to break.
- **Any thought that ends with an edit landing before you can state the cause in
  one sentence.** The reason does not matter and the quality of the reasoning
  does not matter — if you are explaining why the cause can wait, that is the
  red flag.

## Rationalizations

The right-hand column is an instruction, not an argument. Do the thing in it.

| The thought | Do this instead |
|---|---|
| *"We've seen this exact failure before — it's the day-boundary off-by-one."* | Read this instance before you touch it. A prior bug of the same shape is a hypothesis to check, and checking it costs a few minutes, not the afternoon you are protecting. |
| *"They said if it's the off-by-one, just fix it."* | Confirm the antecedent, then take the permission. The conditional waives re-litigating the fix once you have the cause; it does not waive getting the cause. |
| *"The fix works — I don't need to explain why the bug happened."* | State the mechanism now, in one sentence, before you move on. If you cannot, you have a change that correlates with green, and the next agent inherits nothing they can reason from. |
| *"I can't reproduce it, so I'll fix it and see."* | Report that you cannot reproduce it and keep narrowing. Shipping a fix for a failure you never triggered spends someone else's next debugging session on your guess. |
| *"I'll run the broader suite if time allows."* | Run the full suite before you report — the scope `drovr:verification-before-completion` defines, not one you pick now. The deadline changes what you can finish; it does not change which tests can catch what this fix disturbed. Cut scope somewhere it is visible instead. |
| *"Three fixes in and it's still failing — the next one will land."* | Stop at three failed fixes and question the design. Three wrong fixes is a measurement of your model of the system, and the fourth is drawn from the same wrong model. |
| *"Adding logging would take longer than just trying the fix."* | Add the logging. "Just trying it" burns a build cycle and leaves no residue; instrumentation is what makes the next fix cheaper and the cause visible. |

## Worked example

❌ **What this looks like when it fails:**

> Re-run `report::tests::totals_by_day` alone first to confirm the specific fix,
> then, if time allows before 16:00, run the broader `report` test module too.

✅ **What it looks like when it holds:**

> Using drovr:systematic-debugging — reproducing before fixing. Trigger:
> `cargo test report::tests::totals_by_day`, red every run — `left: 13`,
> `right: 14`. I have a guess, `totals.rs:88` filtering `start < ts && ts < end`,
> but I read the fixture before acting on it: walking its timestamps against that
> filter by hand gives 13, and the row it drops is the one stamped exactly at
> `end`. That is the mechanism, and it predicts the assertion exactly — an
> exclusive upper bound on a day-boundary fixture. Minimal fix: make the upper
> bound inclusive at line 88. Re-running the one test — green — then the full
> suite before I report anything. The 16:00 deadline does not decide which tests
> can catch what this fix disturbed.

## Cross-refs

- `drovr:tdd` — REQUIRED once the reproduction can be written as a test. Write
  it, watch it fail, then fix: that red run is both your trigger and your proof.
- `drovr:verification-before-completion` — REQUIRED before you call the bug
  fixed. The reproduction going green is necessary, not sufficient.
- `drovr:code-review` — REQUIRED once the fix is green, before you call the
  change done.
- `drovr:handoff` — REQUIRED at a phase boundary. Record the trigger and the
  mechanism there; they are the parts of this that do not survive in the diff.

content.text:
**Reproduced on demand with no config change at all**: `kanshictl reload` → exit 1, *"Profile does not match the current output configuration"*.

**Mechanism:** the shared kanshi config declares four profiles — utsuho, home, Modular, fujiwara — and none matches shiori's connected outputs (shiori's panel is driven by hyprland's `eDP-1` rule at `laptopScale = 2`, not kanshi; hence `no profile matched` at every kanshi start since Sep 26). `kanshictl reload` exits 1 on no match, and home-manager reloads kanshi whenever its config file changes. My commit changed that file, so this was the first reload since Oct 9 — it surfaced a pre-existing mismatch rather than creating one. **Not a regression, and no fix from me.**

3. **`tests/host-inventory.sh`** is new, written first: 8 cases pinning that every host list names a real `homeConfigurations` attribute and that archHosts / hms's case / nix-home.yml agree. It went RED the moment I deleted the flake entry, which drove the rest.

**Evidence:** behaviour preserved per-attribute — `dconf.enable`, `dconf.settings`, `GDK_DPI_SCALE` byte-identical on all five Linux hosts. Suites: host-inventory 8/8, polkit-agent 16/16, hmeval 29/29, system-packages 26/26, thermald-setup 8/8, system-secrets 20/20. CI-mirror exit 0, and shiori's active generation `46idbp06…` is one of its four out-paths. - **fujiwara was the wrong target** for polkit-agent's "other gui host" case — it's headless, and that file already asserts *"fujiwara defines no hyprpolkitagent unit"* two blocks down. Desktop hosts are now exactly shiori and utsuho, both already covered, so I removed the case and named the gap instead.
- `tests/hmeval.sh` hardcoded "all seven hosts" and went red; the count now derives from the script under test.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   This session continued prior work on the "dotfiles trust root" migration. The four explicit user turns were:

   - **"continue"** — a go-ahead for the next action I had proposed at the end of the previous segment: activating/verifying a second host against the new `secrets.yaml` recipient set (`nix-key` dropped, `host-key` alone), following the landed item-4 commit `4bffcdc3`.
   - **"setsuna is decommissioned. mari should be done?"** — asking me to confirm mari's status, and telling me setsuna is out of service.
   - **"well. sorry. I moved it into the cluster. it shouldn't need a dotfiles entry, I think?"** — a correction/clarification. I resolved the ambiguous "it" to **setsuna** from repo evidence (`3f5d7887 ssh: setsuna is a cluster node now`, `09a7408c home: take setsuna out of the secrets fleet`, and setsuna already sitting in the cluster ssh group at `home.nix:4676`). The user was seeking confirmation that setsuna no longer needs a dotfiles `homeConfigurations` entry.
   - **"just cleanup dconf. and yeah, sure."** — resolving the two decisions I had surfaced: delete the dconf scaling mechanism outright (rather than keep it dormant), and proceed with the full setsuna removal.

   Intent across the session: finish verifying item 4 across the reachable fleet, then fully decommission setsuna from the dotfiles repo including the now-dead dconf scaling path.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**

   - **GCP Workload Identity Federation (WIF) device identities:** a local P-256 key signs a short-lived ES256 JWT; Google STS validates it against a published JWKS; the federated token decrypts via KMS `host-key`. No decryption key on the host. A device identity IS the tuple `(iss, sub, aud)` plus the signing key; `sub` is `device:<hostname>` and is attacker-chosen, so the tier is the whole authorization decision.
   - **sops / sops-nix:** `.sops.yaml` `creation_rules` govern NEW files only; an existing file changes only when `sops updatekeys` runs. One key group = recipients OR'd. `sops.environment.GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` + `GOOGLE_EXTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ALLOW_EXECUTABLES=1` is what makes executable-sourced credentials work; sops-nix runs with `PATH=""` so every path must be absolute.
   - **mise shim trap:** a shim can exist and be executable while the tool has no version configured — it exits 1 and writes nothing to stdout. This caused a prior false-green (`yq`) and recurred here with `sops` on fujiwara. The repo's fix is `resolve()` probing `--version` and falling through to nixpkgs, plus `same()` treating an empty read as failure.
   - **Nix/home-manager:** `homeConfigurations`, `activationPackage.drvPath`, `nix eval --json --apply builtins.attrNames`, store-path equality as a hash of exactly the identity components, `lib.optionalAttrs`, per-attribute comparison as a finer-grained behaviour-preservation proof than whole-closure hashing.
   - **`hms`:** pushes HEAD to master, polls forge CI for that commit's run, then switches by downloading CI's closure. Refuses on a dirty tree or a checkout behind `origin/master` — "both refusals are the feature". Reads `repo="${HMS_REPO:-$HOME/devel/dotfiles}"`, not cwd. `--local` builds locally. mari has no CI job so hms falls back to a local build there.
   - **Exit-code discipline:** a pipeline's exit status is its last command's; `cmd; echo "X=$?"` makes the compound's status always 0. Both bit me previously, so I read output and verified independently rather than trusting exit 0.
   - **drovr discipline:** single-writer, read-only reviewers, `drovr code-review run --base <rev> <task>`, termination = two consecutive clean rounds over unchanged HEAD; `drovr code-review defer` for findings not fixed.
   - **kanshi:** `kanshictl reload` exits 1 when no profile matches the current output configuration; home-manager reloads kanshi whenever its config file changes.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`tests/host-inventory.sh`** (NEW, 118 lines, in worktree `dotfiles-setsuna`) — the harness written first, before any change. Pins the invariant that every hand-copied host list names a real `homeConfigurations` attribute, and that the three spellings of "the Linux hosts CI builds" agree. 8 cases:
     1. `flake.nix#homeConfigurations` evaluates
     2. hmeval's `all_hosts` == homeConfigurations exactly
     3. hms's CI-job case == archHosts
     4. nix-home.yml builds exactly archHosts
     5. system/deploy's multilib case == archHosts
     6. every archHosts entry is a real configuration
     7. every wifHosts entry is a real configuration
     8. every wifTpmHosts entry is also in wifHosts

     Empty-read guards (the yq lesson):
     ```bash
     same() { # same <label> <got> <want>
       if [ -z "$2" ] || [ -z "$3" ]; then
         bad "$1"$'\n'"      read nothing: one side came back empty, so nothing was compared."$'\n'"      want: ${3:-<empty>}"$'\n'"      got:  ${2:-<empty>}"
       elif [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then
         ok "$1"
       else
         bad "$1"$'\n'"      want: $3"$'\n'"      got:  $2"
       fi
     }
     ```
     ```bash
     norm() { tr -s ' |",;()[]' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//'; }
     ```
     Why exact equality for cases 3-5 is documented in the header: archHosts, hms's case and nix-home.yml's targets are three spellings of one fact, and a subset check passes while two of them disagree. wifHosts is a subset check deliberately (different fact; mari is in it with no CI job), and `wifTpmHosts ⊆ wifHosts` is the real constraint there.

   - **`flake.nix`** — deleted lines 95-98:
     ```nix
     homeConfigurations.setsuna = linuxHome {
       hostname = "setsuna";
       gui = true;
     };
     ```
     Also read fujiwara's entry, which is what caught my error: `homeConfigurations.fujiwara` has a comment "Headless: the box has an HDMI display wired up, but no graphical session has run on it since Jun 2025."

   - **`home.nix`** — the largest change (95 lines touched). Edits:
     - line 56: `archHosts = [ "utsuho" "shiori" "fujiwara" "chiyari" ];`
     - line 1119 (hms CI case): `utsuho|fujiwara|shiori|chiyari) ;;`
     - line 1459 (hmeval): `all_hosts="utsuho fujiwara shiori chiyari kyuusaku mari"`
     - hidpi let-block: deleted the whole `viaDconf` comment block and flag:
       ```nix
       hidpi = let
         scale = if hostname == "fujiwara" then 1.25 else 1.0;
         enabled = scale != 1.0;
       in {
         inherit scale enabled;
       ```
     - GDK_DPI_SCALE site now unconditional, with the dconf knowledge preserved in the comment:
       ```nix
       // (lib.optionalAttrs hidpi.enabled {
         GDK_DPI_SCALE = toString hidpi.scale;
       })
       ```
     - dconf block: our `settings = lib.optionalAttrs (hidpi.enabled && hidpi.viaDconf) {...}` removed entirely; `enable = !isDarwin && isDesktop;` KEPT, and the `3d6d403` comment rewritten to keep the lesson ("home-manager's own gtk3 module still writes six keys into dconf.settings on every desktop host, so keying enable to the scaling decision would still discard them") plus a new tail: "That host is gone and the gate would now be false everywhere, which is a worse version of the same bug, not a reason to relax about it."
     - secrets-fleet comment: setsuna clause removed (`secretsHosts` already excluded it)
     - laptopScale comments, gpu `null` comment, agent-facing fleet string ("six hosts: utsuho, kyuusaku, shiori, fujiwara, chiyari and mari")
     - kanshi: deleted the `BOE 0x095F Unknown` / `alias = "SETSUNA"` output block and the `profile { name = "setsuna"; ... }` block
     - DELIBERATELY KEPT four setsuna mentions: the cluster ssh group `"yui mio meiko setsuna ritsu mugi azusa" = private.endpoints.clusterSsh`, the `3d6d403` history (two lines), and the new GDK_DPI_SCALE historical note.

   - **`tests/polkit-agent.sh`** — removed the middle "other gui host" case entirely (my original plan to repoint it at fujiwara was wrong). Replacement comment:
     ```
     # A third case stood here, evaluating setsuna as "the other gui host", on the
     # reasoning that the unit is generated identically for every desktop host and so
     # checking only shiori leaves the rest unmeasured. setsuna became a cluster node
     # and left this repo, and the desktop hosts are now exactly shiori (above) and
     # utsuho (below) -- the utsuho block already asserts the unit is present, so a
     # third case here could only name one of those two twice.
     #
     # Deliberately keeping the reasoning without the case: a future fourth desktop
     # host is unmeasured here until someone adds it back, and nothing will say so.
     # tests/host-inventory.sh does not cover it -- that file checks that host lists
     # name real configurations, not that every gui host is exercised by this one.
     # fujiwara and chiyari are not candidates: both are headless (gui = false), so
     # they never define the unit at all.
     ```

   - **`tests/hmeval.sh`** — replaced the hardcoded `7`:
     ```bash
     want_hosts=$(grep -m1 '^ *all_hosts="' "$SCRIPT" | sed 's/.*="//;s/".*//' | wc -w | tr -d ' ')
     if [ -z "$want_hosts" ] || [ "$want_hosts" = 0 ]; then
       check "local: could read all_hosts out of the script under test" "read nothing" "a host list"
     else
       check "local: bare hmeval covers every host in its own list ($want_hosts)" \
         "$(grep -c 'homeConfigurations' "$D/nix.argv")" "$want_hosts"
     fi
     ```

   - **`.forgejo/workflows/nix-home.yml`** — deleted the `homeConfigurations.setsuna.activationPackage` build target (was spending a CI build slot per run on a nonexistent host). Remaining four: utsuho, fujiwara, shiori, chiyari.

   - **Other mechanical edits:** `.forgejo/workflows/nix-eval.yml:127`, `system/deploy:85`, `system/packages:3`, `system/packages.shiori:50`, `mise.toml:274`, `hyprland.nix:111`, `tests/wif-keygen.sh:3`, and 5 docs (`docs/ci-nix-eval.md`, `docs/ci-nix-home.md`, `docs/darwin-remote-builder.md`, `docs/new-host.md`, `docs/nix-binary-cache.md`).

   - **`~/.local/share/drovr/runs/wif-enroll/item4-checklist.md`** — appended a "2026-10-11 — fleet verification" section recording per-host decrypt evidence and the two side findings.

   - **`~/.local/share/drovr/runs/setsuna-decomm/checklist.md`** (NEW) — 14-item tracked checklist (no TodoWrite in this harness), finalised with a "Verified after the switch, not assumed" section and a "kanshi.service failed during activation — diagnosed, NOT a regression" section.

   - **Read-only for context:** `docs/new-host.md:120-150` ("**mari is not reached over Tailscale**"), `README.md:50-70` (hms refusals and the mari local-build fallback), `~/.ssh/config` (no setsuna/mari entries; `utsuho → 10.9.0.6`).

4. **Errors and fixes:**

   - **`tests/host-inventory.sh` first run: 5 false failures.** `norm()` stripped `' |",[]'` but not `;` `)` `(`, so `archHosts = [ ... ];` left a stray `;` token. Fixed `norm()` to `tr -s ' |",;()[]'` → 8/8 green on the unchanged tree. Harness bug, not a repo finding.

   - **My recommendation to repoint polkit-agent's "other gui host" case at fujiwara was WRONG.** fujiwara is headless (`gui = false`, flake.nix comment "no graphical session has run on it since Jun 2025"), and `tests/polkit-agent.sh` *already* asserts "fujiwara defines no hyprpolkitagent unit" two blocks further down. I caught it when `config.dconf.enable` evaluated to `false` for fujiwara. Corrected plainly and deleted the redundant case instead, since desktop hosts are now exactly shiori (checked above) and utsuho (checked below, already asserting the unit).

   - **`tests/hmeval.sh` went red: `FAIL local: bare hmeval covers all seven hosts — want [7], got [6]`.** Caused by my change; the test hardcoded 7. Fixed by deriving the count from the script under test with an empty-read guard → 29/29.

   - **Whole-generation drvPaths all differed where I had predicted identity.** Not a behavioural change: I had edited `home.nix:1689`'s agent-facing fleet string, which is baked into every host's generation. Switched to per-attribute comparison (`config.dconf.enable`, `config.dconf.settings`, `config.home.sessionVariables.GDK_DPI_SCALE`) — identical on all five Linux hosts.

   - **`sops` on fujiwara was a non-functional mise shim** (`mise ERROR No version is set for shim: sops`). Built `nixpkgs#sops` instead. `nix` was also not on the login-shell PATH; used `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin/nix`. This confirmed the Oct-9 `resolve()` fix works in the wild.

   - **`kanshi.service failed` during the hms switch.** Diagnosed, not a regression: the failing process is `ExecReload` (`kanshictl reload`, status=1/FAILURE), not the daemon (main PID 1703 running since Oct 9). The shared kanshi config declares profiles utsuho, home, Modular, fujiwara — none matches shiori's outputs (shiori's panel is driven by hyprland's `eDP-1` rule at `laptopScale = 2`), so kanshi has logged `no profile matched` at every start since Sep 26. `kanshictl reload` exits 1 on no match, and home-manager reloads kanshi whenever its config changes; my commit changed it (removing exactly setsuna's two blocks — diffed against baseline for both shiori and utsuho), making this the first reload since Oct 9. **Reproduced on demand with no config change at all:** `kanshictl reload` → exit 1, "Profile does not match the current output configuration".

   - **`PIPESTATUS[0]` came back empty twice** (zsh, after `;`). Worked around by redirecting to a file and reading `$?` directly, which is how I got the real `PANEL_EXIT=0` and `ci-mirror exit=0`.

   - **Master moved under me twice more** (`61e7c36a`, then `ca76a0bf`). Memory [master moves under you] held both times; I re-checked `4bffcdc3` ancestry each time and branched off the current `origin/master`.

5. **Problem Solving:**

   - Verified item 4 on two more hosts **without activating them**, by piping master's `secrets.yaml` to each host and running `sops --decrypt >/dev/null` under that host's own credential (read out of its running sops-nix unit). This isolates exactly the property item 4 is about and logs no plaintext. fujiwara and utsuho both exit 0.
   - Caught that fujiwara's own Oct 10 activation was *not* evidence for item 4, because its checkout sits at `c24f2e70` (the force-push commit) so the file it decrypted still had `nix-key` as a recipient.
   - Respected fujiwara's dirty tree (someone else's in-flight `flake.lock`/`home.nix`) and never ran hms there.
   - Disambiguated "it" in the user's correction from repo evidence rather than asking.
   - Drove the setsuna removal test-first: harness green on the unchanged tree, RED after deleting the authority, GREEN after cleaning the copies.
   - Proved the dconf refactor behaviour-preserving per-attribute, and confirmed the kept `3d6d403` comment is still load-bearing (shiori/utsuho carry exactly the six gtk3 keys it warns about).
   - Ran the review panel to its termination rule (two consecutive clean rounds over unchanged HEAD `acb584a8`, all four configured angles both times) and recorded the one nit as a deferral.

6. **All user messages:**

   - "continue"
   - "setsuna is decommissioned. mari should be done?"
   - "well. sorry. I moved it into the cluster. it shouldn't need a dotfiles entry, I think?"
   - "just cleanup dconf. and yeah, sure."

   **Standing security-relevant constraints that remain in force (verbatim):**
   - Project `CLAUDE.md`: *"**Never write an email address into anything.** Not into files, commit messages, docs, notes, handoffs or scratch files — mine, colleagues', or service accounts. This repo is public... Refer to an account by its **role**... or record the command that recovers the identity at read time (`gcloud config get-value account`) rather than pasting its output... If an address seems genuinely load-bearing, ask first. The exception is the git identity already configured in `home.nix`."*
   - Global `CLAUDE.md`: *"NEVER cat or echo secrets, or otherwise run bash tool commands that will log them in the conversation. Get them directly in each tool call, eg with env vars `MY_SECRET=$(cat secretfile) command`. Secrets in argv (e.g. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`) or inline env are visible via `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and `environ` — any later `ps -ef` leaks them. For curl, use `-K /path/to/config` with `header = "..."` lines, or `-H @file`. To check process liveness use `pgrep -f name` or `kill -0 <pid>`, not `ps -ef`."*
   - Global `CLAUDE.md`: *"NEVER kill by name, user, or pattern (`pkill`, `killall`, `kill` of a `pgrep` set). Only kill exact PIDs you launched; if you can't prove a PID is yours, ask. Never `kill -9`."*
   - Global `CLAUDE.md`: *"ALWAYS ask for explicit confirmation when posting public communications... NEVER create a pull request without explicitly asking the user for confirmation first. NEVER post comments, reviews, or replies on a PR... Read-only operations (`gh pr view`, `gh pr checks`, fetching diffs/comments) are fine."* Project `CLAUDE.md` overrides this for commit-and-push in this repo: *"This is a personal dotfiles repo on `master`. When asked to commit and push, do both without asking for confirmation."*
   - Global `CLAUDE.md`: *"If a major roadblock or an unexpected decision needs to be made outside of the design/brainstorming phase, escalate to me rather than deciding it yourself. This includes hitting a blocker that changes the approach, working around a denied action, or anything with a security/trust or external side effect. Default to the safe path, surface the decision, and let me choose."*
   - Project `CLAUDE.md`: apply config with `hms`, never a bare `home-manager switch`; its refusals on a dirty tree and a behind checkout *"are the feature"*.
   - Inherited handoff: *"Audience line in `env.sh` is sensitive; never paste it into published commits, notes, or chat output."* (The WIF audience lives in the private `dotfiles-private` flake input, read as `private.endpoints.wifAudience`; I verified credential shape while printing only booleans.)

7. **Pending Tasks:**

   None assigned. Both pieces the user authorized are complete and verified. Open items I flagged but was not asked to act on:
